skills.name: adr-workflow
skills.summary: Establish and maintain Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) in software repositories.

skills.name: ai-ml
skills.summary: Building AI/ML systems — engineering an LLM or foundation-model application (prompts, tool calling, evals) or running a machine-learning project from framing to deployment.

skills.name: architecture
skills.summary: Any software architecture or design question — ADRs, DDD, C4 diagrams, coupling/cohesion analysis, microservices, component design, fitness functions, SQL schema design.

skills.name: architecture-pattern-advisor
skills.summary: Choose a repository's architecture — topology (monolith, modular monolith, microservices, serverless) or code organization (layered, by-domain, hexagonal, clean/onion), not generic project setup.

skills.name: c4-modeling
skills.summary: Diagram how a software system fits together at Context, Container, Component, Landscape, Dynamic, and Deployment level (not Code / level 4).
skills.compatibility: No dependencies — Mermaid renders natively on GitHub, GitLab, VS Code, and most Markdown tools. Optionally C4-PlantUML for publication-grade output when PlantUML (Java) or a Kroki server is available.

skills.name: communication-analysis
skills.summary: Analyze or rewrite a message, feedback, or conversation with Schulz von Thun's four-sides model and Rogers-style active listening.

skills.name: coupling-cohesion
skills.summary: Assess an existing codebase's coupling and cohesion — module cohesion and LCOM, codebase-wide coupling metrics and zones, or whether a single dependency is balanced (Khononov).
skills.compatibility: The bundled scripts are stdlib-only Python 3.8+. LCOM analyzes Python (precise, via AST), R, and Bash (heuristic); the coupling and balance checks are language-agnostic. Dependency-graph extraction uses whatever tool fits the ecosystem (examples below for Python, JS/TS, Java, .NET, Go).

skills.name: ddd
skills.summary: Domain-Driven Design end to end — strategic subdomain classification and context mapping, tactical pattern choice, and implementation conventions for aggregates, value objects, and events.

skills.name: documentation
skills.summary: Producing technical documentation for a named reader — README, API reference, runbook, architecture doc, or onboarding guide.

skills.name: fitness-functions
skills.summary: Automate a CI check that governs an architecture characteristic — modularity, layering, coupling, security, resilience — and fails the build when it erodes.

skills.name: html-artifacts
skills.summary: Produce a self-contained HTML file instead of a markdown reply when the content has spatial, comparative, or interactive structure.

skills.name: hypertrophy-training
skills.summary: Evidence-based hypertrophy programming and auto-regulation with precise stop criteria, for experienced trainees.

skills.name: llm-application-engineering
skills.summary: Guide the engineering of a foundation-model application across three linked decisions.

skills.name: logical-component-design
skills.summary: Decompose a NEW system or feature into named logical components; to measure an existing decomposition use coupling-cohesion instead.

skills.name: microservices-design
skills.summary: Design or review how services interact — boundaries, coupling, communication style, contract versioning, sagas, resiliency patterns.

skills.name: ml-project-lifecycle
skills.summary: Guide a machine learning project from problem framing through model selection to production deployment.

skills.name: natural-planning
skills.summary: Walk a project through GTD's Natural Planning Model (purpose -> outcome -> brainstorm -> organize -> next actions) to turn a vague, stuck, or overwhelming project into concrete physical next actions.

skills.name: oss-scouting
skills.summary: Scout one third-party open-source repository for open issues that suit a small, clean contribution, and write repro, root-cause analysis, fix diff, test, and a submit checklist to a local folder only.
skills.compatibility: Requires git and the GitHub CLI (`gh`, read-only). Running a candidate's reproduction needs that project's own toolchain.

skills.name: problem-first-explanation
skills.summary: Output-form skill for technical explanations — forces every explanation to start with the concrete problem the concept solves, before the abstract solution or implementation.

skills.name: refactoring
skills.summary: Finding where refactoring is worth starting in a codebase nobody knows well — ranks files by git churn (hotspots) and says how to read the ranking.

skills.name: repo-status
skills.summary: Generate a standup / status update from recent development activity — yesterday/today/blockers, turning rough notes or connected-tool activity into a shareable update.

skills.name: sql-schema-design
skills.summary: Give database consumers a stable interface so physical storage can change without breaking their queries — views as the contract, named CTE pipelines, deployment gates against schema drift.

skills.name: stakeholder-update
skills.summary: Writing a status update for readers outside the immediate working group — leadership, cross-functional partners, or customers — where the audience and the update type decide the shape.
